summary: Nani Gopal Majumdar was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1916–1920). He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and Superintendent of the Indian Museum's Archæological Section (~1929–1938).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1980–1985). He served as an assistant and lecturer at Tohoku University (~1985–1993) and became a professor at Koyasan University (~1994).

Naoki Nabeshima is a Buddhist studies scholar. Attested in 2004, he served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Ryukoku University, where he also founded the Open Research Center for Humanities, Science and Religion.

Naoko Nishimura is an Indologist who earned her PhD from Tohoku University by 2002, studying under Toshifumi Goto. As of 2012, she held an appointment as a specialized researcher at Tohoku University.

Naomi Appleton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who earned her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. She was a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at Cardiff University and joined the School of Divinity at the University of Edinburgh.

Naoshiro Tsuji (1899–1979) was an Indologist and linguist educated at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford. He served as Professor and Chair of Sanskrit at the University of Tokyo (1927–1960) and later directed Toyo Bunko (1974).

Naoya Funahashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He has held appointments at Otani University, attested in 1981, and as a research fellow with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

Narada Maha Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Benedict's College, University College, Colombo, and under Pelene Siri Vajirañāṇa (~1917–1955). He served as Superior of Vajiraramaya Temple from ~1955 to 1983.

Narayan Hemandas Samtani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi (1957–1961), where he was also a research fellow, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Banaras Hindu University (~1961–1984).
Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was a scholar in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Indology. He held an academic post at the University of Calcutta from ~1967 to 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato is an historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned his PhD from the University of Calcutta. He served at the CEACS (~1987–1996) and was a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1996–2011).
Narimoto Tamayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Taisho University, with his tenure attested in 1974 and 1988.

Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held an affiliation at Harvard University (attested 2001) and was appointed professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1975) under Stephan Beyer. She also studied under Ngawang Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Legden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who completed her studies at the University of Michigan (1999–2006). In 2006, she took up a post at the University of Toronto.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley (attested 2008) and became Assistant Professor at UCLA (attested 2016).

Natasha Reichle is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley under Joanna Gottfried Williams, having also studied under Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between ~2012 and 2018 under the supervision of Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin was a historian of science and Sinologist educated at MIT and Harvard. He taught at MIT (1966–1977) before serving as Professor of Chinese Culture and of the History of Science at the University of Pennsylvania (1977–2006).

Nathan W. Hill is a linguist, Tibetologist, and Sinologist who studied at Harvard University (~2001–2009). He served as reader at SOAS University of London (~2008–2019) and became Sam Lam Professor in Chinese Studies at Trinity College Dublin in 2021.
